source: Five additional user photographs of the Passaporte para Português glossary, visible entries apresentar–desde and preceding-page fragments
normalization_notes: Visual transcription of all readable Portuguese glossary rows, including visible preceding-page fragments. No words inferred from missing pages between the photographed pages.
Source references such as 35, P3 and AC are metadata, not CEFR labels or category names.
Lowercase NFC word forms, no punctuation, no whole expressions. Noun-gender articles after commas are removed. Actual articles/prepositions inside phrases remain words.
Expand bom/boa, beijo/beijinho, cem/cento, dele/dela and deles/delas. The o/a gender annotation after artista, cliente, colega and concorrente does not create distinct spellings.
Retain the lexical compounds bem-disposto and bem-vindo; split the attached reflexive pronoun in deitar-se into deitar and se.
Keep real contextual words in parentheses, such as bilhete, telefone and escadas; discard generic algo/alguém and fazer algo placeholders under deixar.
Retain inflected words such as cheia, clássica, aérea, batatas, fritas and caves, and the conjugated forms está, estás, é and compreendo, without inventing new lemmas.
Preserve German glosses as photographed; independently translate individual Portuguese components, not the entire phrase.
The reference beside comissário is transcribed as the visible P1; its row clearly identifies the flight-attendant meaning.

enrichment.translations: Assistant English/Ukrainian translations for new words; existing translations preserved exactly. German meanings remain in the extracted file.
enrichment.levels: Assistant A1/A2 estimates for new words, not levels supplied by the book; existing CEFR levels preserved.
enrichment.groups: Existing topic and grammatical category names only. No textbook or batch provenance categories.

dictionary_checks.note: Verified the photographed spelling and studio/workshop meaning.
Verified the espresso sense; the source German parenthetical double is not copied to the word cheia, which means full.

Existing no translation preserved; sentence-negation sense retained in JSON for review.

translation_notes: caves means cellars/basements, not English caves; borrego includes animal and meat senses.
carioca identifies a person from Rio de Janeiro; it is not a synonym for all Brazilians.
comissário is translated with the contextual flight-attendant sense explicitly marked.
cumprimentos means greetings/regards in the photographed expression; not English compliments.
Preserve lexical compounds bem-disposto and bem-vindo; deitar and se retain separate existing records.
Standalone components are translated independently: bomba is pump/bomb, not the entire petrol-station expression; código is code, not postcode.
